page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rewrite the fraction and differentiate once
steps.margin_note: First mark. Either method is accepted — the quotient rule gives the same −2/(4x + 5)². Check the division before using it: ½(4x + 5) + ½ = 2x + 2.5 + 0.5 = 2x + 3.
steps.memory_tip: A linear over a linear is always a constant plus a constant over the same linear. In that form each differentiation is one chain rule on a power.
lines: Write the numerator in terms of the denominator:
Differentiate once, by the chain rule on the power:

recall.must_convey: That y is rewritten as ½ + ½(4x + 5)⁻¹ (or the quotient rule is used), giving dy/dx = −2/(4x + 5)².
accept: split it as a half plus a half over four x plus five
the quotient rule gives the same first derivative
d y by d x is minus two over four x plus five whole squared
numerator ni denominator terms lo rasi split cheyyali
the inner derivative four comes out each time
heard_as: minus two over four x plus five squared

steps.why: The quotient rule gives the same first derivative, but it would then have to be used again on a squared denominator. Splitting the fraction into a constant plus a power turns both differentiations into one chain rule each.
common_mistakes: Using the quotient rule with a plus sign in the numerator, writing 2(4x + 5) + 4(2x + 3).
Forgetting the inner derivative 4 that comes from 4x + 5.

steps.label: Differentiate a second time
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two minus signs multiply to a plus, so y″ is positive wherever 4x + 5 is positive. Check at x = 0: 16/125 = 0.128.
steps.memory_tip: Each differentiation multiplies by the power and by the inner 4. Here (−2) × 4 = −8, and −2 × (−8) = 16.
lines: Differentiate again by the chain rule:

accept: differentiate the power minus two again
minus two times minus two times four is sixteen

malli chain rule vaadithe sixteen by four x plus five cube
the power goes from minus two to minus three

steps.why: The power drops from −2 to −3 and the chain rule brings out another factor of 4. The two minus signs cancel each other, so the sign of y″ follows the sign of (4x + 5)³.
common_mistakes: Losing one of the two minus signs and writing −16/(4x + 5)³.
Forgetting the inner 4 the second time and writing 4/(4x + 5)³.
